newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish think tank blasts government plan for mines.
newsitem.headline: Polish think tank blasts government plan for mines.

text.p: The Polish government should close loss-making coal mines rather than pump public money into their restructuring and use the savings to retrain workers and create jobs, an independent think tank said on Thursday.

Jan Macieja, a senior official on the Adam Smith Centre's privatisation committee, told a news conference the government's strategy aimed at a gradual reduction of output combined with pit modernisation was ineffective and too costly.
"The mining sector has received the largest amounts of money of all restructured industries and it has been wasted.....(it) is in the worst situation of all sectors," Macieja said.
He said the governmnent should radically cut excess capacity by closing all but 25 to 30 of the most efficient mines, about half the number of mines now operating, and then start real restructuring.
He said the remaining mines should sign long-term supply contracts with power plants and be able to cover domestic demand of about 95 million tonnes annually.
Over a few years, the government should phase out coal mining subsidies.

The government's economic council earlier this month approved plans to reduce coal output by 25 million tonnes annually from the current 135 million tonnes and cut employment by 80,000 to about 170,000 by the year 2000.
Under the scheme, domestic consumption of hard coal, Poland's main source of energy, would amount to about 98 million tonnes annually.
The plan assumes closing only nine mines and privatising two of the most modern mines.
